title: Ram Kishor v. State of U.P. and others
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Mahesh Chandra Tripathi, J.; Vivek Kumar Singh, J.
disposition: Writ disposed of; petitioner relegated to clause 6.8.
headnote: A writ challenging a recovery citation in a theft and unauthorized-use matter was not entertained. The Division Bench held that clause 6.8 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is an efficacious alternative remedy, left the petitioner to that recourse, and hoped the competent authority would proceed strictly in accordance with law.
facts: Ram Kishor filed a writ petition in the Allahabad High Court challenging a recovery citation dated 20 August 2022 issued by respondent no. 3. The State and counsel for the distribution licensee appeared. Counsel for the licensee raised a preliminary objection that the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is a complete code and that, the dispute relating to theft and unauthorized use of electricity, the petitioner had an efficacious remedy of appeal under clause 6.8 of the Code.

holding_units.topic: alternative remedy for theft/UUE recovery citation
holding_units.holding: A writ against a recovery citation arising from theft and unauthorized use of electricity will not be entertained where clause 6.8 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005 furnishes an efficacious remedy; the consumer is left to that recourse and the competent authority is to proceed strictly in accordance with law.
holding_units.flag: Court described clause 6.8 as an 'appeal' for a matter of 'theft and unauthorized use' without identifying a sub-clause.

principle_tags.application: Writ against a theft/UUE recovery citation was not entertained because clause 6.8 of the Supply Code, 2005 was held to be an efficacious appeal/recourse.
Challenge to the 20.8.2022 recovery citation was disposed of on the clause 6.8 alternative-remedy objection without examining the assessment on merits.

not_decided.point: Validity of the recovery citation dated 20.8.2022
not_decided.note: Merits of the theft/UUE recovery were not examined; the writ was disposed of on the alternative-remedy objection.
